text:
anya: Quick heads-up — ran a seeded annotated smoke pass comparing the new vector candidate 'syrinx-v0.3' (FP16 -> 8-bit per-tensor quant) against our baseline 'beacon-v1' on the short-seq holdout (queries <= 16 tokens). summary below.

anya: TL;DR: overall recall@5 is roughly equivalent (+0.7%), but short-seq recall@1 drops ~0.08 (0.58 -> 0.50) which is bigger than we'd expect. cluster silhouette down slightly (0.41 -> 0.37).

matt: Can you paste the command / config used? was batching or prefix caching different?

anya: sure — ran with our standard eval harness: 
```
./eval_vectors --model syrinx-v0.3 --quant config=per_tensor,8bit 
  --holdout seeded_shortseq.json --k 1,5 --metrics recall,silhouette --seed 42
```
Batching = 1 (to mimic online latency), no prefix cache.

reza: Interesting — do we have the per-query breakdown? Is the drop concentrated on very short (<=6 token) queries?

anya: yes, breakdown by length:
- 1-6 tokens: recall@1 baseline 0.49 -> syrinx 0.35 (large drop)
- 7-12 tokens: baseline 0.59 -> syrinx 0.55
- 13-16 tokens: baseline 0.68 -> syrinx 0.66
So the biggest delta is concentrated on the ultra-short bucket.

tara: any idea if quantization or the model changes are causing it? did you run FP16 (non-quant) for comparison?

anya: FP16 run included: FP16 syrinx-v0.3 recall@1 shortseq 0.46 — still below beacon 0.49 for 1-6 tokens but closer. so quantization amplifies the gap (0.46 -> 0.35). suggests model architecture/embedding norm + quantization interplay.

matt: Could be L2 norm shift after quantization. do we see cosine mean shift across buckets?

anya: mean cosine to positives (1-6 tokens): baseline 0.74 -> syrinx-FP16 0.71 -> syrinx-8bit 0.63. distance to nearest negative increases slightly.

reza: That points at scale collapse after quant. Try per-channel 8-bit (if supported) — per-tensor is aggressive. Also try symmetric vs asymmetric quant configs.

anya: good call. I'll run per-channel 8-bit + asymmetric. queued a run now (ops-bot id below).

ops-bot: eval-run queued: id=evr-20260321-7789 (per-channel, asym, seed 42).

tara: Also add a small human-annotated seed set check — those ultra-short queries are often ambiguous; maybe the annotation agreement is low and the metric is brittle. can we compute NDCG and top-k agreement?

anya: on it. early NDCG@5 looks similar across models; top-1 agreement with annotators for 1-6 tokens: baseline 0.62, syrinx-FP16 0.57, syrinx-8bit 0.43. so it tracks.

matt: Ok — action items: (1) try per-channel/asym quant and report numbers; (2) run small calibration post-process (embedding L2 renorm / temperature) to see if simple fix recovers; (3) if still bad, block promotion for short-seq-sensitive customers. can we get plots?

anya: will produce length-bucketed barplots + cosine distribution violin by model and attach to the eval ticket. also will run L2 renorm and a small scalar calibration sweep (0.9-1.1).

reza: add a quick clustering sanity: t-SNE of shortseq anchors + negatives to visually inspect collapse.

anya: noted. I expect to have updated numbers and artifacts in the eval ticket ~2-3 hours.

tara: thanks. also ping engineering docs/networking so that if we need to recommend per-channel quant for this model we capture the tradeoffs.

matt: thanks anya. :thumbsup:

anya: thanks all — will update thread when per-channel run completes.
